title: Executors
engine: jupyter
jupyter: python3
depends-on: extend/adapters

Executors are a contrib invention for implementing backend behavior behind an
[AdapterBase](adapters.qmd) adapter. Core dispatches only to an adapter
executable; it neither discovers executors nor imports `ExecutorBase`.

## Registry, discovery, and lowering

Executor lookup uses `(MyExecutor.adapter, MyExecutor.name)`, not the entry-point
key. The authoring name can differ from the resolved target: `batch` under
`lambda` resolves to the deployed `lambda_uri` and `dml-lambda-adapter`.

<!-- docs:pseudocode: This metadata belongs in an installable executor distribution. -->
```toml
[project.entry-points."daggerml.contrib.executors"]
example_backend = "my_package.executor:ExampleExecutor"
```

```{python}
from daggerml.contrib.status import status


executor_keys = {item["key"] for item in status()["executors"]}
assert {"local:script", "local:docker", "local:ssh"} <= executor_keys
```

## Dispatch and lifecycle

`ExecutorBase` creates a fresh instance for each call. Durable continuation must
therefore be returned as state, not retained on the instance. Repeated invoke
requests perform polling; there is no wire `poll` operation.

```{python}
from daggerml import Runnable, Uri
from daggerml.contrib.executors import ExecutorBase


class ExampleExecutor(ExecutorBase):
    name = "example"
    adapter = "example"

    @classmethod
    def resolve_runnable(cls, uri, kwargs, sub):
        return Runnable(target=Uri(uri), kwargs=kwargs, sub=sub, adapter="example-adapter")

    def start(self, cache_key, execution_id, runnable, remote, scratch_uri):
        assert remote["root"] == "s3://example/root"
        return {"status": "retry", "adapter_state": {"job": "1"}, "error": None}

    def poll(self, cache_key, execution_id, runnable, state, remote, scratch_uri):
        return {"status": "retry", "adapter_state": state, "error": None}


payload = {
    "operation": "invoke", "cache_key": "cache", "execution_id": "execution",
    "remote": {"root": "s3://example/root"}, "runnable": {"target": {"uri": "example"}},
    "adapter_state": None, "scratch_uri": "s3://example/scratch",
}
assert ExampleExecutor.handle(**payload)["adapter_state"] == {"job": "1"}
assert ExampleExecutor.handle(**{**payload, "adapter_state": {"job": "1"}})["status"] == "retry"
```

This illustrates resolve-and-dispatch, not a complete deployable backend.
Later calls may come from different processes or repositories; continuation
must support safe status checks rather than repeated launches.

The runtime owns result publication and lifecycle/cache updates. Required
teardown belongs in `cleanup`, not only terminal polling: publication can stop
further invokes. Cleanup must not alter the result, and returning a result does
not wait for cleanup retries.

Return `cancelled` only after confirmed teardown, not merely an accepted
termination request. The runtime owns the transition to `canceled`; retain state
and retry while teardown is incomplete.

## Backend implementation and built-ins

Script workers receive function source plus explicit `extra_objs` and
`post_lines`, not the authoring module's imports or globals. Put dependencies
inside the function or inject them explicitly.

Script and Docker handles belong to their launching user and host. Foreign
callers retry without touching local resources; hosts and containers must have
distinct hostnames. Ownership is not authentication or automatic failover.

Docker and Batch own wrapper resources independently of their nested adapter's
outcome. Their nested `--poll` driver retains child continuation through cleanup.
SSH forwards continuation to its destination; Batch has no local ownership
restriction.

Use the supplied remote scratch URI for detached input/output. Runtime records
own execution coordination; `S3Store` under `remote.root/data/` is for artifacts.

## Batch submission recovery

Batch writes submission intent to `lambda:batch/submission.json` under execution
scratch before calling `SubmitJob`, with SDK retries disabled for that call.
The record binds the execution, remote root, scratch path, resolved queue,
job name, definition ARN, and submission search bound. Explicit throttling
retains the definition for another submission; ambiguous outcomes only observe.
All submission continuations are checked against execution/remote/scratch identity
before polling or teardown. Failed intent writes roll back known-unsubmitted
definitions and retain their handles if rollback fails.

Recovery scans one `ListJobs` job-name-filtered page per invoke, including terminal
jobs, and verifies candidates through `DescribeJobs`. State retains pagination
and every matching ID. One match resumes normal polling; multiple matches report
failure with all IDs retained for cancellation/cleanup. Teardown waits for every
tracked job to become terminal before deregistering its definition.

An empty discovery result cannot authorize resubmission. A crash after intent
persistence but before submission, jobs no longer discoverable, inaccessible
queues, or persistent identity mismatches can therefore leave an unresolved
retry requiring operator investigation. Keep scratch records until teardown.
Recovery is not an exactly-once guarantee: a discovery scan can miss a duplicate
that becomes visible later. The search bound allows one minute of clock skew.

The Lambda role needs scratch S3 read/write, job registration/submission/tagging,
`DescribeJobQueues`, `ListJobs`, `DescribeJobs`, termination, and deregistration
permissions. Moto coverage proves control-plane recovery, not production IAM or
container execution.

## Batch isolation

`AWS_EC2_METADATA_DISABLED` is not a sandbox: job code can unset it or request
metadata directly. EC2-backed Batch operators must block container access to
host IMDS, including IPv6 when enabled. For Docker bridge networking, install
these rules before admitting work and persist them across reboot:

<!-- docs:pseudocode: Run only on an operator-owned Batch ECS host using Docker bridge networking; the documentation fixture does not administer hosts. -->
```sh
iptables -I DOCKER-USER 1 -d 169.254.169.254/32 -j DROP
ip6tables -I DOCKER-USER 1 -d fd00:ec2::254/128 -j DROP
```

Other network modes need the corresponding ECS IMDS block. IMDSv2 alone is not
container isolation. Preserve ECS task credentials at `169.254.170.2`, scope
the task role to required remote/scratch prefixes, and restrict `iam:PassRole`
to that role. Do not use host networking or privileged containers for untrusted
work. EC2-backed containers share a kernel; mutually untrusted workloads need
separate compute boundaries.

Moto verifies control-plane requests and S3 handoff, not container execution,
IAM enforcement, or network isolation. Verify IPv4/IPv6 IMDS requests fail and
task-role S3 access succeeds inside a real job before claiming isolation.
See AWS's [task role isolation guidance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/task-iam-roles.html)
and [IMDS credential provider settings](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sdkref/latest/guide/feature-imds-credentials.html).
